catalog_quote: 4. The tonic accent is strongly marked as a rule, but not always. It falls on the penultimate syllable of every word with very few exceptions: e. g. (a) The final vowel may be accented for emphasis. (b) There are a few enclytics which draw the accent on to the last syllable of the preceding word, as ke, mu: e. g. Nyumbáni, at the house. Nyumbaní mu, within the house. (c) There are a few accented monosyllables, as dwè, only; bi, utterly. (d) In certain words the final vowel is accented and prolonged, or repeated: e. g. the pronouns denoting an object more distant than the person addressed, as— yulée and yuleyaa, yonder.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress ('tonic accent') falls on the penultimate syllable of every word; exceptions are emphatic final stress, enclitic-induced shift to the word-final syllable, a few stressed monosyllables, and a few pronouns with stressed lengthened final vowels.
new_statements.exceptions: (a) final vowel may be accented for emphasis; (b) a few enclitics (ke, mu) draw the accent onto the last syllable of the preceding word; (c) a few accented monosyllables (dwé 'only', bi 'utterly'); (d) certain words, e.g. distal demonstrative pronouns, have an accented and prolonged or repeated final vowel (yulée, yuleyaa 'yonder').
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level ('every word'); notes phrase-level effects: enclitics ke, mu shift the accent to the last syllable of the preceding word (Nyumbáni 'at the house' vs Nyumbaní mu 'within the house'), and demonstrative suffixes alter the position of the tonic accent (sec. 22, va vaNdúwa). No tone is described; the 1902 grammar predates recognition of Bantu tone, so 'tonic accent' here = penultimate stress/length prominence of the Southern Bantu type (cf. Gowlett 2003 sec. 3.6 zone-level statement).
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source describes Xilenge (Lenge), Glottolog dialect leng1257 under chop1243; Junod 1927 (Bantu Studies 3: 59) warns that Smyth's Xilenge 'is not the language of the people commonly called Chopi, but a kind of combination of Tshopi and Thonga', and Maho 2009 lists the Lenge dialect as possibly extinct. The penultimate-accent statement is nonetheless consistent with the zone-wide Southern Bantu penultimate length-stress reported by Gowlett 2003 (sec. 3.6) for all Zone S languages except Lozi. No first-hand statement for Chopi proper (Copi/Cicopi) was opened.

new_statements.rule_in_words: A strongly marked 'tonic accent' falls on the penultimate syllable of every word. Exceptions: final vowel accented for emphasis; the enclitics ke and mu pull the accent onto the final syllable of the preceding word (Nyumbáni vs. Nyumbaní mu); a few monosyllables carry accent (dwè 'only', bi 'utterly'); in distal demonstrative pronouns the final vowel is accented and lengthened or doubled (yulée, yuleyaa). Sec. 22 adds that monosyllabic demonstratives suffixed to a noun become part of the word 'and so altering the position of the tonic accent' (i.e. the accent stays penultimate in the enlarged word). No statement about tone or pitch anywhere in the book (a full-text search for stress/accent tone/pitch/intonation: only 'to pitch' in the dictionary).
new_statements.exceptions: (a) emphatic final-vowel accent; (b) enclitics ke, mu shift accent to the final syllable of the host; (c) accented monosyllables dwè, bi; (d) distal demonstratives with accented, prolonged/repeated final vowel (yulée, yuleyaa); sec. 22: suffixed demonstratives shift the accent position within the enlarged word.
new_statements.identity_note: The work describes Xilenge (Lenge), which Glottolog lists as the dialect Lengue [leng1257] under chop1243; its title page calls it 'the language of the people commonly called Chopi, spoken on the east coast of Africa between the Limpopo River and Inhambane'. Junod (1927, Bantu Studies 3: 59, held by the project) calls Smyth's Xilenge 'a kind of combination of Tshopi and Thonga', so the statement is strictly about the Lenge variety rather than Chopi proper.

tone.quote: A fonologia suprassegmental é a que se preocupa com os aspectos que afectam mais do que um segmento tais como a silaba, o acento, o tom; enquanto a fonologia segmental vai-se preocupar com o estudo dos sons vocalicos e sons consonanticos. Para o presente trabalho incidir-nos-emos na fonologia segmental, isto é, no estudo das vogais e consoantes da lingua Copi, incluindo as regras que regem a sua combinacao na formacao de unidades maiores (morfemas, palavras ou mesmo frases).
tone.translation: Suprasegmental phonology is concerned with aspects that affect more than one segment, such as the syllable, accent, tone; whereas segmental phonology is concerned with the study of vowel and consonant sounds. For the present work we will focus on segmental phonology, i.e. on the study of the vowels and consonants of the Copi language, including the rules governing their combination into larger units (morphemes, words or even sentences).
